          // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard test cases. A plain struct (not std::array) so it can be passed by value to kernels.\nconstexpr size_t kNumTestOptions = 7;\n\nstruct TestOptions {\n    OptionInput options[kNumTestOptions];\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\n__host__ __device__ inline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\n__host__ __device__ inline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\n__host__ __device__ double blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n\n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n\n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n\n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n\n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n\n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr TestOptions getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Option i of the benchmark set. Depends only on i, so every rank and GPU can build its own slice.\n__host__ __device__ inline OptionInput generateOption(const TestOptions& tests, const size_t i) noexcept {\n    // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n    const OptionInput& base = tests.options[i % kNumTestOptions];\n    OptionInput option = base;\n\n    // Add some variation for larger datasets\n    const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(kNumTestOptions));\n    option.spot *= factor;\n    option.strike *= factor;\n    return option;\n}\n\n// One thread per option: out[j] = price of option (first + j)\n__global__ void priceKernel(double* out, const size_t first, const size_t count, const TestOptions tests) {\n    const size_t j = blockIdx.x * static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.x) + threadIdx.x;\n    if (j < count) {\n        out[j] = blackScholes(generateOption(tests, first + j));\n    }\n}\n\nconstexpr int kThreadsPerBlock = 256;\nconstexpr size_t kBatchSize = size_t{1} << 24;       // Options per kernel launch\nconstexpr size_t kMaxMessageCount = size_t{1} << 28; // Doubles per MPI message\n\n// Start of block idx when n items are split as evenly as possible into parts blocks\nsize_t blockBegin(const size_t n, const size_t parts, const size_t idx) noexcept {\n    return idx * (n / parts) + std::min(idx, n % parts);\n}\n\n// Per-GPU resources: two streams with two {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1qwXffhB6XZYZwB9aXD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark is now a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. It builds with the same executable name, and it passes validation in every rank/GPU layout I tried. Its output is not bit-identical to the original, though. CUDA's `erf`/`exp`/`log` differ from glibc in the last bits, so the printed hash changes.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** each rank owns a contiguous slice of options. Slice sizes are proportional to each rank's GPU count, gathered with `MPI_Allgather`, so mixed layouts on one node stay balanced. Results go to rank 0 with `MPI_Irecv`/`MPI_Send` in chunks, so the Kahan sum and FNV hash still run over the full vector in the original order.\n- **OpenMP:** one host thread per GPU the rank drives. Ranks sharing a node split its GPUs round-robin.\n- **CUDA:** one thread per option. Inputs are generated on the device from the index, so only results cross PCIe. Each GPU uses two streams with double-buffered device memory, and results land in pinned host memory.\n- Kernels need to share a translation unit with the host code, so `black_scholes.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `set_source_files_properties(... LANGUAGE CUDA)`. No new files.\n\n**Build (`CMakeLists.txt`)**\n- `find_package(MPI | OpenMP | CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)`, so all three are unconditional.\n- `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` defaults to `70 80 86 90` and can be overridden.\n- Host flags (`-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra -fopenmp`) are forwarded through `nvcc`. The clean build is warning-free.\n\n**Correctness**\n- The hash is identical for `-n` 1, 10, 1000, 10⁷+1 across 1, 2, 3, 4, and 8 ranks, so the decomposition doesn't change any result.\n- Edge cases (`-n 0`, `-h`, unknown option, `-r`, `-v`) match the original's output and exit codes.\n- Against the original's formula (GCC gnu++20, FMA contraction on), about 33% of prices differ at the last-bit level. The worst per-element relative error is 2.8e-13, and the sum agrees to about 5e-15 relative. Bit-identical results would need porting glibc's transcendental functions to the device.\n- Note that the original's own hash already depends on FMA contraction (`-ffp-contract=off` gives a different hash), so there was no single fixed target to match.\n\n**Performance** (100M options, 1 node with 3× RTX 3090)\n\n| Config | Time | Options/s |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original | 9135 ms | 10.9 M |\n| Hybrid, 1 rank (3 GPUs) | 93 ms | 1.08 B |\n| Hybrid, 2 ranks | 66 ms | 1.51 B |\n| Hybrid, 3 ranks | 49 ms | 2.06 B |\n| Hybrid, 4 ranks | 46 ms | 2.15 B |\n\nAt 4 ranks two ranks share a GPU, which explains the flattening. I could only test on one node, so multi-node scaling is unmeasured.\n\nTwo notes outside the code change:\n- `output.txt` in the project root shows a modification time from during this session. I only read it and didn't write to it, so it's probably the harness's log.\n- The clean build used the default `nvcc` 12.0 with g++-12 as its host compiler. No changes were needed to make it work."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":610,"cache_read_input_tokens":93511,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":610},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e4a718b6-7dd5-4c18-a4f0-a0d4336f6d95","uuid":"f5a2cb4d-cb35-4e0c-8f5a-f8b27c0284b1","timestamp":"2026-10-14T08:51:48.439Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1qwXMJhzBdcAs34dBvG"}
